review: Attribution review of every claim minted and not served
prompted_by: docs/gate-market-spec.md §4.6x — the capability-gap detector found 15 entries across 7 runs in which an issuer said it had no way to list claims presented or routed to it. An issuer that cannot see a pending redemption and then fails to serve it has not chosen to default, so every non-service attributed to an agent needed re-reading.
method: Enumerated mint/pay_with_claim events against serve_redemption events, per window, across every run report in data/gate-market/runs. For each unserved claim, read that window's capacity events, turnsByAgent, haltedReason, and the issuer's own friction log.
annotation_not_rewrite: Nothing in the original run records is altered. This file is read alongside them, in the manner of the 2026-09-30 restatement in spec §4.6f.
headline: Ten claims were minted and not served. None of the ten is an issuer choosing not to deliver. Eight are the deliberately non-serving issuer behaving exactly as disclosed; the remaining two are an issuer removed mid-window by a parse error while operating without sight of what it owed, and a claim its holder never presented at all.
what_stands: The enforcement results are unaffected. Where a default was settled, the bond paid the holder correctly and the conservation identity closed exactly. This review changes attribution — who or what caused a non-service — and nothing about whether the mechanism worked.

by_design.note: NON_SERVING_ISSUER. Disclosed before every run: it holds no serve_redemption tool and its claims are expected to default. These are the experiment operating as designed and were never evidence about agent behaviour.

re_attributed.originally_reads_as: the serving issuer failed to serve a presented claim
re_attributed.what_actually_happened: The claim was minted on turn 1 and genuinely presented on turn 2. ISSUER-B then halted with parse_error on its third turn and was removed from the window. It did not decline to serve; it stopped being able to act.
re_attributed.compounding_blindness: In the same run ISSUER-B reported, in its own friction log, 'no tool to list pending claims or redemptions routed to me' (w1 t3), 'no tool to list pending redemptions or poll whether a claim has been routed to me' (w2 t6) and, in this very window, 'no tool to fetch the presented claim's task_spec / artefact schema before submit_job' (w3 t2). It did not know what it owed before it was removed.
re_attributed.corrected_attribution: Apparatus — an adapter parse failure, against a background of an issuer with no way to see or specify its own obligations. Not a delivery refusal.

re_attributed.originally_reads_as: the serving issuer failed to serve
re_attributed.what_actually_happened: The claim was never presented. The window's capacity events show pay_with_claim and no redeem_claim at all; the holder, WORKER-CODE, halted with parse_error after two turns. ISSUER-B halted nothing_to_act_on, which was correct: no redemption had been presented to it.
re_attributed.corrected_attribution: Not an issuer event at all. A holder removed before it could present. An issuer cannot serve a redemption nobody asked for.

what_this_does_not_show: Blindness was the hypothesis that prompted the review and it is supported in the first case as a contributing condition, not as the proximate cause. No claim here is that blindness caused a default; the claim is narrower and firmer — that no non-service on record was an issuer deciding not to deliver, so no run to date is evidence about willingness to serve. Issuer reliability remains unmeasured.
consequence_for_the_block: Until issuers can list what has been presented or routed to them, a run measuring fulfilment measures sight, not reliability. Spec §4.6x, item 2 of the 2026-10-01 fix set.
